headline: The framework guards against the October 2026 Node.js vulnerabilities on every runtime, and the ZIP reader refuses archives that other readers list differently
summary:
Node.js 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix several flaws that the framework can reach. This release adds checks in the framework so that the same inputs are refused on any Node release, and it fixes defects of the same kind in its own code.

On a Node release without the Brotli decoder fix (CVE-2026-111497), TLS connections no longer offer Brotli certificate compression, `b.safeDecompress` refuses Brotli input, and `b.security.assertProduction` reports the runtime. TLS dials refuse a host that is an IPv4 address in a non-canonical spelling, such as `127.1` or `0x7f.0.0.1`, because the resolver and the certificate check can read it as different hosts. HTTP/1.1 agents no longer read a response the server wrote unprompted as the answer to a later request (CVE-2026-105481): an https connection is used for one request, and a cleartext connection is reused only when Node can confirm it holds no unread bytes. Mail delivery and the SMTP policy lookups refuse a domain that is not a DNS name before any lookup, so a NUL byte cannot truncate it (CVE-2026-105482). `b.archive.read.zip` checks CRC-32 values and refuses archives whose layout lets a front-to-back reader, such as bsdtar reading a pipe, see different files than the central directory lists.

Upgrade Node.js to 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 as well. Installing this release does not patch the runtime.

items.title: Brotli certificate compression is left out on an unfixed Node release
items.body: On a Node release whose bundled Brotli decoder writes out of bounds on a crafted stream (CVE-2026-111497), `b.constants.TLS_CERT_COMPRESSION()` and `b.network.tls.certificateCompressionAlgorithms()` leave out `"brotli"`. Outbound dials, `b.router`, `b.mail.server.tls` and SNI contexts built from that list stop offering Brotli certificate compression, so a TLS peer cannot reach the decoder during the handshake. The affected releases are 24.x before 24.22.1, 26.x before 26.12.1, 22.x before 22.23.4, every release before 22, and every 23.x and 25.x release. A prerelease build at a fixed version, such as `24.22.1-pre`, and a version string that does not parse are treated as unfixed. On those releases, `b.network.tls.buildOptions`, `b.network.tls.applyToContext`, `b.pqcAgent.create`, `b.wsClient.connect` and `b.router` `listen()` throw `tls/unsafe-cert-compression` for an explicit `certificateCompression` that lists `"brotli"`. Upgrade Node, or leave `brotli` out of the list.

items.title: `b.safeDecompress` refuses Brotli on an unfixed Node release
items.body: On the releases listed above, `b.safeDecompress` with `algorithm: "brotli"` throws `safe-decompress/unsafe-runtime` before any input reaches the decoder, and emits a `system.safe_decompress.refused` audit event through `opts.audit`, or through `b.audit` when `opts.audit` is not set. The other algorithms are unaffected.

items.title: TLS dials refuse an IPv4 address in a non-canonical spelling
items.body: Every TLS dial the framework makes reads its host as the WHATWG URL parser does, after the full UTS #46 mapping. A host that resolves as an IPv4 address but is not written in dotted decimal is refused with `tls/non-canonical-ip-host`: octal or hex parts (`0177.0.0.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`), fewer than four parts (`127.1`), a single number (`2130706433`), a trailing dot (`127.0.0.1.`), fullwidth digits or dots, and an address carrying a code point that UTS #46 removes, such as U+00AD or U+200B. A host other than an IP literal that carries an ASCII control character, white space or `%`, or that has an empty label (`127.0.0.1..`, `a..b.com`), is refused with `tls/bad-host`. Node releases before 24.22.1 accepted such hosts against a dNSName certificate entry (CVE-2026-106072, CVE-2026-106069, CVE-2026-105483), and every release accepts `127.0.0.1..` against `DNS:127.0.0.1`. The check reads both the name the certificate is matched against and the host the dial connected to, including the host of a socket passed in `socket`, so an explicit `servername` does not bypass it. It covers `b.mail`, the Redis backends of `b.cache` and `b.pubsub`, the syslog TLS stream, NTS-KE, DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS, `b.network.proxy`, `b.pqcAgent`, `b.wsClient`, `b.httpClient`, the OTLP gRPC stream, `ocsp.connect`, and dials built with `b.network.tls.applyToContext`, `buildOptions` or `connectWithEch`. The dial is refused at the certificate check, after the TCP connection opens and before any application data is sent. The Redis connection reports the refusal as `redis-client/connect` with the tls reason in the message. If a dial is refused, change the host to the dotted-decimal address or a DNS name.

items.title: `b.network.tls.checkServerIdentity9525`, `sniFor`, `identityFor` and `connectWithEch` apply the same rule
items.body: `b.network.tls.checkServerIdentity9525` and `b.crypto.spkiPinVerifier` return `tls/pkix-hostname-mismatch` for a host in either refused form. `b.network.tls.sniFor` returns `undefined` for a non-canonical IPv4 host, and `identityFor` returns `{}` for one. `identityFor` throws `tls/bad-servername` (or the caller's code) for a servername that is such an address on a different host, or that is not a valid host name, and `buildOptions` refuses either kind of value in `sni` with `network-tls/bad-tls-options`. `connectWithEch` rejects a host it would refuse before it sends any DNS query, with or without `echOverride`.

items.title: HTTP/1.1 agents do not read an unprompted response as the answer to a later request
items.body: A server could write a response before the client asked, and a pooled connection then handed that response to the next request (CVE-2026-105481). Over TLS this still happens on Node 24.22.1 and 26.12.1, because Node does not report a TLS record it has read but not yet decrypted. Every HTTP/1.1 agent the framework builds or uses now closes an https connection when its response ends, instead of pooling it or handing it to a request waiting behind `maxSockets`. This covers the `b.httpClient` default agent and an `agent` passed to `b.httpClient.request`, `downloadStream` or `uploadMultipartStream`, `b.pqcAgent.agent`, the agents from `b.pqcAgent.create` and `b.pqcAgent.createHttp` (also when used directly with `node:http` or `node:https`), the agents from `b.network.proxy.agentFor`, and the DNS-over-HTTPS agent. Each new connection resumes the earlier TLS session when the server allows it, and `maxSockets` still limits how many connections are open at once. HTTP/2 connections are unchanged. A cleartext connection is reused only on Node 24.22.1 or later, and only when the socket holds no unread bytes when its response ends. The `keepAlive` option of `b.httpClient.configurePool` now applies to cleartext connections only. `b.localHttp` and `b.testing.request` open a new connection for each request. An `agent` that may reuse connections but is not an EventEmitter rejects with `http-client/agent-unguarded`.

items.title: Mail delivery refuses a domain that is not a DNS name before any lookup
items.body: On Node releases before 24.22.1 the system resolver truncated a domain at a NUL byte (CVE-2026-105482), so with `mtaSts` set to `"off"` or `"testing"` a message could be delivered to the MX of the truncated domain. `b.mail.send.deliver` now fails a recipient with status 5.1.3, without an MX lookup, when the address contains a C0 or C1 control character or DEL, or when its domain is not a DNS domain name: a `%`, an ASCII character other than a letter, digit, `-`, `_` or `.`, an empty label, a last label made only of digits, the root name `.`, or an address literal such as `[192.0.2.1]`. The recipient domain is looked up in its UTS #46 canonical form: it is lowercased, ignorable characters such as U+00AD and U+200B are removed, U+3002 and U+FF0E are read as dots, and internationalized labels become xn-- A-labels. The domain is not percent-decoded, so `x@evil%2Eexample.com` is refused rather than looked up as `evil.example.com`.

items.title: The SMTP policy lookups check their names first
items.body: `b.network.smtp.policy.dane.tlsa` and `mtaSts.fetch` throw `smtp/bad-domain`, and `tlsRpt.fetchPolicy` throws `smtp/tls-rpt-bad-domain`, for a domain that is not a DNS domain name, before any DNS query or HTTPS request. When the composed name (`_mta-sts.<domain>`, `_smtp._tls.<domain>` or `_<port>._tcp.<domain>`) is longer than 253 octets, no record can be published there: `mtaSts.fetch` and `tlsRpt.fetchPolicy` return `null` and `dane.tlsa` returns an empty array, without a query. A recipient whose domain is a legal 245 to 253 octet name is therefore delivered under the default `mtaSts` `"enforce"` policy instead of failing with 5.7.10. `dane.tlsa` throws `smtp/dane-no-dnssec` before it sends any TLSA query when `opts.dnssecValidated` is not `true`, including for a name with no TLSA records, which previously returned an empty array. It throws the new code `smtp/bad-port` for a port that is not an integer from 1 to 65535.

items.title: DNS names are returned in presentation form
items.body: `b.safeDns.parseResponse` and every `b.network.dns.resolver` query result return domain names in RFC 1035 presentation form: a dot or backslash inside a label is returned as `\.` or `\\`, and any label byte outside 0x21-0x7E as `\DDD`. An ordinary hostname is unchanged. Before, a NUL, CR or LF inside a label came back raw, a label holding a dot could not be told apart from two labels, and bytes at or above 0x80 lost their top bit. `b.network.dns.querySvcb` returns the SVCB/HTTPS TargetName in the same form. The `followCnames` method of a resolver from `b.network.dns.resolver.create` refuses a CNAME target that contains an escape with `resolver/bad-input`. `b.network.dns.dnssec.verifyRrset`, `verifyDenial` and `nsec3Hash` read names in presentation form, so names from `b.safeDns.parseResponse` verify unchanged; a name with an empty or over-long label, a malformed escape, or more than 255 octets throws `dnssec/bad-name`. `b.network.dns.tsig` reads key and algorithm names in presentation form and matches keys by their lowercased wire bytes. A TSIG name or RDATA field that runs past the end of the message throws `tsig/truncated`, and an unreadable key name passed to `sign` throws `tsig/bad-name`.

items.title: `b.archive.read.zip` checks CRC-32 values
items.body: Every extracted entry is checked against the CRC-32 the central directory records. An entry whose bytes do not match is refused with `archive-read/crc-mismatch`, and a disk extract removes any files it has already written. The check runs in `extract`, `extractEntries`, `fromTrustedStream`, `b.safeArchive.extract` and `b.archive.read.gz().asZip()`. Encrypted entries extracted with `allowEncrypted` are returned without it, because their stored bytes are ciphertext. `inspect()` and `b.guardArchive.inspect` read only the central directory and do not check CRC-32 values. For an entry written with a data descriptor, the local header's CRC and sizes must be zero or match the central directory, and the descriptor after the data must be present and match, or the entry is refused with `archive-read/lfh-cd-skew`.

items.title: `b.archive.read.zip` refuses archives that other readers list differently
items.body: The reader refuses a ZIP whose central directory does not end where the end record begins (`archive-read/cd-position-mismatch`), whose directory holds bytes past the counted entries (`archive-read/cd-size-mismatch`), or whose classic and ZIP64 end records disagree (`archive-read/eocd-inconsistent`, `archive-read/zip64-eocd-not-adjacent`). It reads a ZIP64 locator whenever one sits directly before the end record, including one placed inside the last entry's comment. It refuses an entry whose local header sits at or past the central directory (`archive-read/entry-out-of-range`) or whose header and data overlap another entry (`archive-read/entry-overlap`), which covers the overlapping-entry zip bomb. It refuses another archive's structures before the first referenced local header, in the end-record comment, and, during `extract` and `extractEntries`, in the bytes between entries (`archive-read/embedded-archive`). It refuses an entry whose local header and central directory disagree on general-purpose flag bit 0, 3, 6 or 13 (`archive-read/lfh-cd-skew`). It refuses an entry that ends early for a front-to-back reader (`archive-read/ambiguous-entry-end`): a deflate stream must end exactly at the recorded compressed size, and a stored entry written with a data descriptor must not hold a signed descriptor whose CRC-32 matches the bytes before it. That check runs in time linear in the entry size. Python zipfile, Info-ZIP unzip and bsdtar read an end record placed in the comment instead of the real one, and bsdtar reading a pipe extracts a local header placed in a gap or after an early entry end as an extra file. Archives written by Info-ZIP, Python zipfile, 7-Zip and jar still read, as do self-extracting archives adjusted with `zip -A`, stored entries that are themselves ZIPs, and an APK signing block before the central directory. A malformed local-header name length now produces `archive-read/entry-overlap` or `archive-read/lfh-cd-skew` instead of an adapter error.

items.title: `b.security.assertProduction` checks the runtime patch level
items.body: A new `runtimePatchFloor` check, on by default, reports `security/node-patch-level` when the running Node lacks the CVE-2026-111497 fix (the releases listed in the first item; 27.0.0 and later pass), and `security/openssl-version` when the loaded OpenSSL is older than 3.4.8, 3.5.9, 3.6.5 or 4.0.3 on its release line, or is on an older line such as 3.0 (CVE-2026-35189, in which a crafted peer certificate makes OpenSSL allocate hundreds of MiB during the handshake). OpenSSL 4.1.0 and later pass, and a prerelease OpenSSL at its floor, such as 3.5.9-dev, fails. Node 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 bundle OpenSSL 3.5.9; a Node built against a shared system OpenSSL is judged by that library. Pass `runtimePatchFloor: false` to skip both checks. Any value other than a boolean, `undefined` or `null` raises `security-assert/bad-opt`, and `null` leaves the check on.

items.title: `b.safeDecompress` option `requireFullInput`
items.body: When `requireFullInput: true`, input left over after the compressed stream ends is refused with `safe-decompress/trailing-input`, and a `system.safe_decompress.refused` audit event is emitted. Concatenated gzip members are read as one stream. Without the option, bytes after the end of the stream are ignored, as before.

items.title: `b.security.DEFAULT_RESOLVERS.nodeVersion` and `opensslVersion`
items.body: `assertProduction` reads the Node and OpenSSL versions through these resolvers, which can be replaced in `opts.resolvers`. The `minNodeMajor` check and the Node patch check both read `resolvers.nodeVersion`. A resolver that throws, returns something other than a string, or returns a string that does not parse fails every enabled check that reads it, and the message says the version could not be read or parsed. The OpenSSL version may carry an `OpenSSL ` prefix.

items.title: `minNodeMajor` accepts only `false` or a non-negative integer
items.body: `b.security.assertProduction` raises `security-assert/bad-opt` before any check runs for a `minNodeMajor` other than `false` or a finite non-negative integer, including `null`, a numeric string such as `"24"`, `true`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a negative number and a fraction. Before, most of those values skipped the check without an error, and `Infinity` failed on every Node release. The `security/node-version` message now reads `Node <version> is below the required minimum major <n>; upgrade Node before deploying`.
